Rose Hill #3

Wild Side

Elsie Silver

4.15
298,122 ratings30,221 reviews
Rate this book
Goodreads Choice Award
Nominee for Readers' Favorite Romance (2025)
I’d always dreamed of my wedding day. But not like this. Not looking into the eyes of the man who betrayed me.

But when my nephew’s guardianship is contested, I decide I’ll do whatever it takes to keep him in Rose Hill. Even if it means marrying the enemy.

Rhys Dupris.

A man who is secretive, broody, and completely infuriating. A man whose work takes him away for weeks on end and brings him back covered in mysterious bruises—ones he won’t talk about. In fact, we barely talk at all.

Which would be fine, except when he’s not talking, he’s staring. And the way he looks at me is borderline indecent.

The tension between us has always been palpable. But living under the same roof is a dangerous temptation.

I swore I would never forgive him. But that was before I knew the man behind the mask. The one who’s fierce and protective. The one who’s gentle and patient. The one who shows up for us when we need him most.

He’s not at all who I thought he was.

And that makes hating my husband so much harder… and loving him just a little too easy.

About the author

Elsie Silver

27 books82.4k followers
Elsie Silver is a #1 New York Times bestselling author of sassy, steamy, small town romance. She’s a born and raised Canadian girl who loves a good book boyfriend and the strong heroines who bring them to their knees. Her books promise banter, tension, and a slow burn that comes to a screeching halt.

4.75 stars

”every eye in the stadium is on him. but his eyes are on mine the whole time.”


Elsie Silver paints once again a fresh small-town romance that balances deliciously raw emotions and palpable attraction, blending harmonically grief, love, and the kind of commitment that feels inevitable with a found family plot line.

Tabitha is strong-willed, sharp, and fiercely independent; someone who has learned to stand on her own while taking care of the people she loves. Rhys, on the other hand, is steady, secretive, and sculpted like a warrior. he watches, waits, and understands her in ways she wishes he didn’t. they were never meant to be more than distant acquaintances, linked only by her sister, his close friend. but when tragedy leaves behind a three-year-old boy, Milo, their worlds interlace in a way neither of them predicted. a marriage of convenience sounds as the only way to keep Milo safe and give him the life he deserves.

what initiates as an arrangement infused with tension—Tabitha pushing him away at every turn, Rhys refusing to go anywhere—slowly blooms into something deeper. beneath the resistance is a man completely devoted to her, and a woman terrified of what it means to let him in. and i absolutely loved how the author found the perfect equilibrium in their couple’s dynamic between mooring and the irresistible pull.

i adored how the novel isn’t just a love story; it’s about loss, healing, and finding family in unexpected places. with an undeniable chemistry, heartfelt moments, and a hero who would do anything for the woman and kid he loves, this book is completely engrossing and i couldn’t put it down !

many thanks to Periwinkle Poney & the author for providing and e-ARC in exchange for an honest review!

5 Stars ★

"When I become Wild Side, everything falls into place."


Damn, Elsie has done it again! I swear she is the QUEEN of small town romance, and I will never get enough!

Wild Side is the third installment in the Rose Hill series and is my favorite yet. Small town romance is becoming one of my favorites. It doesn't stop there. It's also a marriage of convenience, which I love and was portrayed so well, another favorite single dad, and slow burn. It is not just a romance, though, but a story following the process of loss, greiving, and healing.

Tabitha crossed paths with Rhys three years ago when he became her sister's landlord. Now, as she grieves the loss of her sister, he approaches her with the news that he has been left guardianship of her nephew. When guardianship is contested, they form a plan to marry until they can figure things out.


Tabitha Garrison works at the local bistro that she owns, and it fits her as she loves taking care of others. I love that Elsie writes such strong fmcs, and she is no exception. She is so strong-willed, fierce, sassy, and sarcastic, and I adore her so much. She goes through great lengths to protect and do anything for her family and loved ones. This was shown with what she went through and did for her sister. She literally did everything that she could to help her when her sister didn't always deserve it. I understand why she did what she did. That protectiveness was always there for her nephew Milo and got even stronger. She would do anything for him, and it shows through her in everything that she does. She is so strong that she's not one to break down, but when she did, I just wanted to wrap her in the strongest hug and hold her.

“I am with my family, Rhys. If I didn’t want to be here with you, I wouldn’t be.”


Rhys Dupris is a professional wrestler who hides himself until he takes on the role of his character. When he's in character, he holds himself more confident and is able to put his insecurities aside. He's not one to open up to people and hides a lot about himself, and he doesn't feel like he deserves many things that he has due to his upbringing. He is so selfless, though, caring, and holds a soft spot for Milo. Their relationship was so cute to watch. I just loved watching him slowly open himself up and show his vulnerabilities. I love a man who can show this side of himself, too bad not many men in real life do. Oh, and the mouth on this man, yes, please! Oh, and Elsie made me fall for another man with the name Rhys.

"Being Wild Side was my ticket out of a tough upbringing, and slipping into character always feels like tugging on a favorite old hoodie. It feels like peace."


Tabitha and Rhys start off with animosity with her constantly trying to push him away while he just stood by and took it, turned into a marriage of convenience, that dipped into a slowly budding relationship. Their sexual tension and banter along the way was everything. The chemistry that these two exuded for one another is off the charts, though it burned slowly while also toeing the line of spicy. I loved the way that he was protective of her and the way that she was always teasing him in a fun, playful way that kept things on the lighter side when it was needed. She showed him that she would be there for him at every turn whether he wanted her to or not, and was worthy of being loved. He showed her the care that she needed even when she didn't think she did or didn't want to take it. They just worked so well together from the very start, even though they didn't know it.

“Thank you, Tabitha.”
“For what?”
“Turning my life from black and white to full color.”
“You did the same for me. I help you find your color, and you help me find mine.”


I swear Elsie writes some of the best found family! I'm such a sucker for it and eat it up every time! I loved seeing West, Skylar, Ford, Rosie, and Skylar once again. The support that they all give to not only Tabby but one another is endearing.

I was a bit worried about the pro wrestling in this one, but it worked for me. And even though I was in a mini slump, I still couldn't seem to put this down. I can always depend on Elsie to help me with a slump and keep me hooked. Now, I'll be over here impatiently the next in the series that has me intrigued.


Favorite quotes and moments

"Rhys Dupris is the carnival ride that I just can’t manage to get off of."

“What’s wrong, husband? You look like you can’t decide whether you want to kill me or fuck me.”

“I pinky promise that no matter what happens, I will never take anything that’s yours.”
“You know these aren’t legally binding, right?”
“Yeah, but only a total asshole breaks a pinky promise.”

Maren’s Reads

February 19, 2025
After the death of her sister, Tabitha is ready to take over custody of her nephew Milo. That is until she finds out her sister’s landlord Rhys, the man she blames for her sister’s downward spiral, has been granted custody. When they form an arrangement to keep Milo close to both of them, the last thing Tabatha and Rhys expect is to want more than a marriage on paper.

Y’all, I cried. And more than once. To me, this is probably the biggest indicator that I not only loved these characters and their story, but that I also felt fully connected to them on a visceral level. I admit that I was reticent about where the story was going. I am not the biggest fan of “marriage of convenience” or wrestling for that matter. However, like Elsie Silver is known to do, she made me love fall in love with this trope similarly to the way she turned a book featuring an accidental pregnancy into one of my favorites.

Each and every character in this story was fully fleshed out, completely relatable, and fully lovable. As a result, it was incredibly hard not to develop a rooting interest in their happiness (hence the crying). Tabatha is such a spitfire. Burdened with untapped feelings over the loss of her sister and her potential involvement, she is still one of the most emotionally intelligent and emotionally mature characters I have encountered of late. She is a boss who shows up for both her people and her baby (the restaurant she worked to build).

Rhys is a little harder to get to know at first. Surrounded by emotional walls of his own making, a result of his upbringing in foster care, Rhys keeps both Tabby and the reader at bay. But as she helps to knock down his walls, allowing all of us to get to know how dynamite this man really is, his vulnerability makes him all the more endearing. Milo and the rest of their friend group where the side characters needed to create the sense of family that shines through in this book. And although I didn’t come away a wrestling fan, I sure did come away a fan of Wild Side and maybe a fan of Little Willy too.

As always, the steam was steaming in this one, although it’s not quite as intense as her others. Every scene fit, but more importantly, Silver creates the tension needed to make their chemistry explode once they do have their doors off the hinges moments, and she does this by not overdoing it or incorporating unnecessary scenes too early. This is probably what I love most about her open door romances, and what sets them apart from others.

🎧 The audiobook is equally fantastic. Helmed by Jason Clarke and Samantha Brentmoor, heavyweights in the narrator community, the characters come to life through their impeccable narration. It’s fun and flirty, but with the emotional impact these two are able to bring to any role.

Read if you like:
▪️marriage of convenience
▪️sports romance
▪️touch her and die vibes
▪️wrestling
▪️foodie romance
▪️cinnamon roll alpha
▪️forced proximity
▪️small town
▪️no third act break up

CW: death by overdose (off page), parental abandonment

i really loved this one. it had such a soft, emotional feel to it that stuck with me even after i finished. it didn’t quite reach five stars, but it was close. wild eyes is still my favorite in the series, but this had so many moments that came close. west still has my whole heart, but rhys is definitely up there now too.

tabitha was such a well-done character. she felt real — guarded and a little tough, but with good reason. she’s been through a lot and it shows in how careful she is with her heart. even when she was being difficult, i understood where she was coming from, and i liked how she always tried to take care of the people around her, even if it meant pushing them away.

rhys was so easy to love. he’s quiet, observant, and shows he cares through actions, not words — which made him feel even more genuine. his bond with milo was so sweet, and i loved how consistent he was when it came to tabitha. he never tried to change her or pressure her, he just showed up again and again until she started to trust him. that quiet loyalty hit hard.

the romance felt slow and intentional, which worked perfectly for their story. there wasn’t any over-the-top drama — it was just two people learning how to lean on each other, figuring out how to turn something unexpected into something real. i also loved the focus on grief and found family — it gave the story so much heart.

Does love start off as obsession?
Because that’s what I am.
Obsessed with my wife.
I can’t get enough of Elsie Silver’s ‘Rose Hill’ series. Each book gets better and better. I’m a sucker for a good marriage of convenience romance, and this exceeded all my expectations.

I have been intrigued by both Tabitha and Rhys since we met them both in previous books. I wasn’t sure what would bring them together, but Tabitha really seemed to dislike Rhys. And it does have an enemies to lovers vibe for a short time. But it doesn’t take long for Rhys to win her over.

Tabby seems like such a baddie, and in a way, she is. But you see a softer side of her when it comes to her nephew, Milo. And Rhys. With time, he gets the soft side of her as well. I loved these two together. They were such an amazing couple. I couldn’t keep the smile off my face as I was reading about them slowly but surely falling for one another.

The romance, the chemistry, the heart… Wild Side had it all. Elsie always slays with her writing and her books are unputdownable. I can’t wait to see what she does next.

I devoured this book and was SO obsessed with the banter between Tabitha and Rhys! Are you kidding me!? 「 ✦“Our family is special. Unique circumstances. Chosen rather than born into. All tied together in an unusual way.”✦ 」


I went into this book with sky-high expectations because EVERYONE says it's the best in the series. And I believed you all… and okay, it's not a bad book, but I prefer the previous one a thousand times more.

book playlist

•packing it up by gracie abrams

•i wish i hated you by ariana grande

⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔

˙∘ও┆𝑷𝒍𝒐𝒕 ★
In this story, we meet Tabitha Garrison, a talented chef at a restaurant in Rose Hill. From a young age, she has carried more responsibilities than she should, caring for her older sister, Erika, the town's outcast who has struggled with addiction for years and dies suddenly from an overdose, leaving behind her young son, Milo.

Tabitha is obviously devastated after the news and blames herself for not noticing the signs that her sister was unwell; but at the same time, she knows she can't succumb to grief because there are things to resolve regarding Milo. And naturally, she assumes that as his aunt, having cared for him for a long time while Erika was still alive, she will also be his guardian.

「 ✦“Everyone around me has been crying. I can’t start too. If I start, I worry I won’t know how to stop. Then shit won’t get done. And that’s my job right now. Take care of her little boy. Navigate my parents’ grief. Run my restaurant. Get shit done. Numb is preferable.”✦ 」


「 ✦“He’s the reason she focused so hard on healing for those few years. And all I knew was that I was happy to see my sister trying. I see so much of my sister in him. And my heart aches that she won’t be here to see him grow.”✦ 」


But that's where Rhys Dupris comes in. He's Erika's tenant and also happens to be Milo's true legal guardian, having been named by her in her will before she died. Rhys is a man with an intimidating appearance and a mysterious, broody personality, with an alter ego that no one knows about: Wild Side, a very famous professional wrestler.

But behind that facade hides a man who grew up without a family and doesn't know how to let love into his life because he believes he doesn't deserve it, yet he's willing to do anything to give Milo what he could never have growing up.

「 ✦“I’m glad Milo has someone like her in his corner. I wish someone had fought as hard for me as she does for him. I may not like her, but I admire her grit and devotion.”✦ 」


「 ✦“Rhys has a way of shutting everyone out. I’m not sure what it is, but something about the moment makes me wonder if the man I married even knows how to let someone love him.”✦ 」


Their paths cross again after Erika's death, and after a few misunderstandings and hidden truths, the animosity between them is palpable. However, they share a common goal: Milo's happiness and well-being.

Thus, after a hasty agreement, they decide to marry and co-parent Milo to ensure he can legally remain in Canada with Tabby. But what begins as an arranged marriage, far from genuine, slowly transforms into a found family that neither of them saw coming and that gives them both a space where they finally feel happy, complete and loved.

However, they still must overcome their own fears, insecurities, guilt, and secrets to stay together.

「 ✦“It’s a team effort. A family effort. It’s a foreign experience. But Tabitha has shown me it’s okay to lean on people. That I’m not a burden. That indeed, they will come back even when it seems inconvenient.”✦ 」


⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔

˙∘ও┆𝒐𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒂𝒍𝒍 𝒕𝒉𝒐𝒖𝒈𝒉𝒕𝒔 ★
I must admit that up until the first half of the story I was HOOKED and thought this book would be my favorite in the series… but then everything fell apart for me.

I liked how the story began with a throwback to when Rhys and Tabby first met and then brought us to the present with Erika's death.

Tabby is the type of person who feels she has to swallow her feelings, keeping them hidden from others, so she doesn't let them fall apart and so she can be the strong one, the one who carries everyone else's burdens. And I admit that reading about all those feelings of pain and guilt she carries because of her sister's death was incredibly difficult; my heart ached for her, and I hoped she could heal and move on.

「 ✦“They say it takes a village, and Erika didn’t have one even though she needed it. So I became her village, taking on as much as I could. I grew to love that kid like he was my own. My parents keep telling me I went above and beyond for her… but wondering if I could have done more will haunt me forever.”✦ 」


And then, learning that Rhys had custody of Milo, by Erika's own decision, hit Tabby like a ton of bricks. It must have felt like all the effort, sacrifice, and time she dedicated to caring for and protecting Milo had been for nothing.

But at the same time, we learn that Erika was also like a little sister to Rhys; and that's why he felt so connected to Milo, because he partly raised him and only wants his well-being and happiness. And having grown up without parents himself, in foster homes where he wasn't treated well, Rhys wants to prevent Milo from suffering the same fate as him at all costs.

「 ✦“I think that’s what I’ve found in Rhys. Someone I can talk to about my sister who also has fond memories of her. I don’t have to be the one who came out on top. I just get to be the girl who lost her sister.”✦ 」


「 ✦“Erika didn’t love Rhys. Not in the way I do. I’ve let go of the guilt and decided I’m not taking anything that was hers or could have been hers. I’m taking one thing for myself after years of giving to everyone else. And I’m not letting him go.”✦ 」


⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔

I want to give a shout-out to the wedding vows, because even though Tabby and Rhys didn't write the vows themselves, I LOVED IT and I feel like it touched some nerves for both of them. Also… the fact that their first kiss is at the altar is chef's kiss, hehehe.

「 ✦“I, Rhys, promise you, Tabitha, to always respect and admire you and to appreciate you for who you are, as well as the person you become.
I promise that your dreams will be our dreams, and that I will do everything I can to make them a reality for both of us.
I promise to be a spectator to your life, a participant in your experiences, and your biggest advocate in every moment.
I promise to allow you space to be those things in my life too.
I promise to support and encourage you, laugh with you in times of joy, and comfort you in times of sorrow.
I promise to cherish and reinforce the love between us in good times and in bad, when life is simple and when it’s complicated—when loving you is easy and when it takes effort.
I promise to be faithful to you and to place you and our family above all else.
I promise to love you completely and unconditionally, today and every day, and to stand at your side always, wherever life takes us together.”✦ 」


Up to that point, I feel that everything was handled well.

⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔

In the second half of the book, I got incredibly bored. Tabby and Rhys's relationship changed almost immediately after the wedding; it was as if they went from rivals to lovers in a single chapter, and I didn't like that. It would have been better if they had developed more of a friendship before all the physical and romantic stuff happened.

Their family dynamic with Milo wasn't shown much either, except for a couple of scenes, and I don't like it when they use a child they have in common to force the "marriage of convenience" trope, only to then abandon it or downplay the importance of that family connection.

After that, everything was really random. I can't explain it, but it's as if the author ran out of ideas on how to move the story forward and made up a lot of filler, especially with Rhys's job, which didn't work to entertain, to speed up the plot, or for anything AT ALL.

⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔⏔ ꒰ 💍💚 ꒱ ⏔⏔⏔
